extortioner. Hebrew. muz. Occurs only here.

oppressors = treaders down. Hebrew. ramas. Occurs only here.

entries.title: in mercy.
entries.content:
in mercy. The burden goes beyond the immediate future to the ultimate future.

mercy = lovingkindness, or grace.

in truth. See note on Isaiah 10:20 .

hasting righteousness = prompt in equity. Compare Isaiah 46:13 .

entries.title: We.
entries.content:
We. Compare Isaiah 6:8 . Genesis 1:26 .

his lies shall not be so = his resources do not correspond.

entries.title: Kir-hareseth.
entries.content:
Kir-hareseth. Some codices read "Kir-harasheth".

stricken = worn away. Hebrew. naka'. Occurs only here.

entries.title: the fields
entries.content:
the fields = [as to] the fields. Compare Deuteronomy 32:32 . 2 Kings 23:4 .Jeremiah 31:40 (feminine).

Heshbon. Compare Isaiah 15:4 .

languish = he [Moab] hath enfeebled.

and = supply [as to] and omit the colon.

the vine of Sibmah = Sibmah's vine.

lords. Probably plural of Majesty for "great lord of the nations", a title claimed by the kings of Assyria.

heathen = nations.

Jazer. Probably Beit Zer'ah, on the east of Jordan (Numbers 32:1 .Joshua 13:25 ; Jos 21:39 . 2 Samuel 24:5 . 1 Chronicles 6:81 ; 1 Chronicles 26:31 .Jeremiah 48:32; Jeremiah 48:32 ).

wandered through: or, strayed into.

entries.title: water thee
entries.content:
water thee = make thee drunk.

Elealeh. See note on Isaiah 15:4 .

the shouting for thy summer fruits and for thy harvest is fallen = on thy summer fruits and thy harvest a war-cry hath fallen,

entries.title: plentiful
entries.content:
plentiful = fruitful.

wine. Hebrew. yayin. App-27 .

presses = wine-vat. Hebrew. yekeb, not gaih. See note on Isaiah 5:2 .

entries.title: sound
entries.content:
sound = make a plaintive sound. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia . Hebrew v'kirbi Kir.

Kir-haresh. See note on Isaiah 15:1 .

entries.title: on.
entries.content:
on. Some codices, with two early printed editions, read "unto": weary with climbing up to. Compare Isaiah 15:2 .

prevail = obtain anything.

entries.title: Within.
entries.content:
Within. Some codices, with two early printed editions, read "about".

three years. From the death of Ahaz.

contemned = brought low.

small = few.

feeble = small.

entries.title: burden.
entries.content:
burden. The second of the seventh burdens.

Damascus. The capital of Syria.

is taken away = is swept away. This was by Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, and the slaughter of Rezin (632. B.C.) See 2 Kings 16:9 , and 2 Kings 7:9 , 2 Kings 7:16 , above.

city. heap. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia ( App-6 ) Hebrew. me'ir. mei .

entries.title: cities of Aroer.
entries.content:
cities of Aroer. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia . Hebrew. arey aro'er .

Aroer. There were three other cities of that name, and this one which is not identified.

entries.title: children
entries.content: children = sons.

entries.title: be
entries.content: be = become.

entries.title: it:
entries.content:
it: i.e. Jacob's glory (Isaiah 17:4 ).

it: i.e. Jacob's fatness (Isaiah 17:4 ).

Rephaim. South-west of Jerusalem. So called after one "Kapha", a mighty one among the descendants of the Nephilim, as Anak was, who gave his name to another branch. See App-23 and App-25 .

entries.title: the LORD God of Israel.
entries.content:
the LORD God of Israel. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 32:27 . Compare Joshua 9:18 , Joshua 9:19 ; Joshua 10:40 , Joshua 10:42 , &c). See note on Isaiah 29:23 .

God of Israel. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 24:10 . Numbers 16:9 ). Occurs in latter part of Isaiah (Isaiah 41:17 ; Isaiah 45:3 ; Isaiah 48:2 ).

entries.title: a man
entries.content:
a man = Literally the man. Hebrew. 'adam. App-14 . I

look = have an eye unto.

have respect = have regard. Note the Alternation in verses: Isaiah 17:7 , Isaiah 17:8 , "look" and "have respect".

the Holy One of Israel. See note on Isaiah 1:4 .

entries.title: the groves
entries.content:
the groves = the Asherahs. See App-42 . Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 34:13 .Deuteronomy 7:5 ; Deuteronomy 12:3 ; Deuteronomy 16:21 ). App-79 .

images = sun images. Reference to Pentateuch (Leviticus 26:30 ); both mentioned again (Isaiah 27:9 ).

entries.title: desolation.
entries.content: desolation. See note on Isaiah 1:7 .

entries.title: Rock.
entries.content:
Rock. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 32:13 ). App-92 .

pleasant plants. Probably = plantings of Adonis.

strange slips: or slips of a strange [God],

entries.title: In the day
entries.content: In the day = By day.

entries.title: people
entries.content:
people = peoples.

noise = booming, or roaring.

rushing. Note the Figure of speech Repetitio ( App-6 ), for emphasis.

entries.title: God
entries.content:
God = One.

chaff = dried grass.

a rolling thing = a galgal. See note on Psalms 83:13 .

entries.title: trouble
entries.content:
trouble = consternation.

he is not: or, he is no more. Some codices, with two early printed editions, Aramaean, Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate, read "and he is no more".

entries.title: Woe
entries.content:
Woe = Ho! The third of the seven burdens.

land. beyond: i.e. land. beyond Abyssinia.

shadowing with wings = of the rustling zalzal (from zalal, to tinkle, compare Deuteronomy 28:42 ).

entries.title: the sea
entries.content:
the sea = the Nile. So called by the inhabitants of the Sudan to-day.

bulrushes = reeds. Not the papyrus, but its companion reed, the ambach, which reaches a height of fifteen feet and has yellow flowers.

scattered and peeled = "tall and smooth-faced".

terrible. They formed the armies of "So" or Sha-baka, and are the backbone of the Anglo-Egyptian army.

whose land the rivers have spoiled: i.e. the "sudd" or swamps (hence Sudan). The Dinka and Shilluk negroes live on the floating cakes of sudd.

entries.title: He
entries.content: He =. Jehovah. See Structure, above.

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

cloud of dew = summer night mist. Hebrew. 'ab. Not a raincloud, which latter is never seen in harvest. Eight times rendered "thick clouds".

entries.title: left.
entries.content:
left. See note on "forsaken" (Isaiah 1:4 ).

fowls. beasts. Note the Alternation.

entries.title: present.
entries.content:
present. Hebrew shai, because of being conveyed. Only here, and Psalms 68:29 ; Psalms 76:11 .

the LORD of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 .

the name. See note on Psalms 20:1 .

entries.title: burden.
entries.content:
burden. The fourth of the seven burdens.

rideth. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia.

entries.title: set the Egyptians, &c.
entries.content: set the Egyptians, &c. Referring to the anarchy consequent on the defeat of Egypt by Sargon (688 B.C.)

entries.title: spirit.
entries.content:
spirit. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

idols. See note on Isaiah 2:8 .

charmers. Hebrew. ittim = mutterers. Occurs only here.

familiar spirits. See note on Leviticus 19:31 . Reference to Pentateuch (Leviticus 20:6 , Leviticus 20:27 ; Deuteronomy 18:11 , &c.) App-92 .

entries.title: cruel lord.
entries.content: cruel lord. Sing, adjective with plural noun = the lord of the nations, as the kings of Assyria called themselves.

entries.title: fail
entries.content:
fail = be dried up. Hebrew. nashath. Occurs only here in "former" portion, and only in Isaiah 41:17 in the "latter" portion. Elsewhere only in Jeremiah 51:30 . App-79 .

the river: i.e. the Nile.

entries.title: they shall turn, &c.
entries.content:
they shall turn, &c. = the arms of the river shall stink.

brooks = canals of Matzor : i.e. Egypt. See note on Isaiah 7:18 .

emptied = shallow.

entries.title: paper reeds
entries.content:
paper reeds = meadows. Occurs only here.

wither = be dried up. and be no more: or, and disappear.

entries.title: mourn.
entries.content: mourn. See note on Isaiah 3:26 .

entries.title: weave.
entries.content: weave. Occurs in the "former" portion only here, and in Isaiah 38:12 ; and in the "latter" portion only in Isaiah 59:5 .

entries.title: purposes:
entries.content:
purposes: or, foundations. Compare Psalms 11:3 .

make sluices. fish: or, work for wages shall be grieved in soul.

fish = souls Hebrew. nephesh, App-13 . margin, "living things".

entries.title: Zoan.
entries.content:
Zoan. See note on Isaiah 30:4 .

fools. Hebrew. aval . See note on Proverbs 1:7 .

entries.title: staggereth
entries.content: staggereth = goeth astray, as in preceding clause.

entries.title: rush.
entries.content: rush. See note on Isaiah 9:14 .

entries.title: In that day:
entries.content:
In that day: i.e. the day when this burden should be fulfilled (not "the day of the Lord "). Note the six steps, verses: Isaiah 19:16 , Isaiah 19:18 , Isaiah 19:19 , Isa 16:21 , Isa 16:23 , Isa 16:24 .

the hand. Put for the judgments indicated by the act.

entries.title: the land of Judah.
entries.content: the land of Judah. The Assyrian armies came through Judah.

entries.title: five cities.
entries.content:
five cities. These were probably Heliopolis, Leontopolis, Daphne, Migdol, and Memphis.

the language of Canaan: i.e. the Hebrew language, by the multitude of Jews that went thither.

destruction. The primitive reading was doubtless hazedek = "righteousness", which the Septuagint simply transliterates, aoeoek . From a desire not to compete with "Jerusalem", which bore this name (Isaiah 1:26 ), it was altered to cheres , which in Chaldee = "the sun", or in Greek = "Heliopolis", which is the reading in many MSS., two early printed editions, and the margins of the Authorized Version and Revised Version But when the temple at Jerusalem was cleansed and restored, the temple at Heliopolis was deemed schismatic; and, by altering one letter (= CH, for = H), cheres (the sun) was altered to heres (destruction). Hence the present reading of the current Hebrew text.

entries.title: an altar.
entries.content:
an altar. See App-81 .

a pillar. Probably a boundary pillar. Hebrew. nazab . A pillar or monument. Not for worship.

at = close to.

entries.title: sign.
entries.content: sign. See note on Isaiah 7:11 .

entries.title: do sacrifice.
entries.content: do sacrifice. "The third Ptolemy, when he had occupied all Syria by force, did not sacrifice thankofferings to the gods in Egypt, but came to Jerusalem and made votive offerings" (Josephus, c. Apion , Isaiah 11:5 ).

entries.title: In that day:
entries.content: In that day: i.e. the glorious future, the day of the LORD. Not the same as Isaiah 19:11 . highway. See note on Isaiah 7:3 .

entries.title: land:
entries.content: land: or, earth.

entries.title: Tartan.
entries.content:
Tartan. A title = commander in-chief.

Sargon. Never once named by classic writers, and in Scripture only here.

entries.title: the same
entries.content:
the same = that.

by = by the hand of.

Isaiah. See note on Isaiah 13:1 .

naked. Put by Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Whole), for being scantily clad.

entries.title: sign and wonder.
entries.content: sign and wonder. Reference to Pentateuch, (see note on Isaiah 7:11 with Isaiah 8:18 ), and App-92 .

entries.title: expectation.
entries.content:
expectation. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the help expected from Egypt.

Egypt their glory. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the Egyptians, in whom they gloried.

entries.title: isle
entries.content: isle = sea coast, or coast land. See note on Isaiah 11:11

entries.title: burden.
entries.content:
burden. The fifth of the seven burdens.

of = relating to. Genitive of Relation. App-17 .

the sea. The waters of the Euphrates in flood were so called, as the Nile was (Isaiah 19:6 ). Compare Revelation 17:3 , Revelation 17:15 .

whirlwinds = storms.

pass = sweep.

entries.title: dealer
entries.content:
dealer = one.

sighing. Caused by the oppression of Babylon.

entries.title: night.
entries.content:
night. A Homonym. Hebrew. nesheph = darkness, here, but daylight in Job 7:4 . 1 Samuel 30:17 . See notes there. The Revised Version, in doubt, renders it here "twilight".

pleasure = joy.

fear = trembling.

entries.title: Prepare, &c.
entries.content: Prepare, &c. Figure of speech Irony. App-6 .

entries.title: a chariot
entries.content:
a chariot = a troop.

a chariot with a couple of horsemen = a troop of horsemen in pairs.

entries.title: Alion: My LORD*.
entries.content: Alion: My LORD*. Read: [as] a lion, "O LORD", &c.

entries.title: men.
entries.content:
men. Hebrew. 'ish. App-14 .

Babylon is fallen, &c. Note the Figure of speech Epizeuxis , for emphasis.

the graven images of her gods. Reference to Pentateuch. Phrase peculiar to Deuteronomy 7:25 ; Deuteronomy 12:3 . App-92 .

entries.title: threshing.
entries.content:
threshing. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause) for the results of it. Here = my oppressed People. Compare Isaiah 41:15 .Micah 4:13 .Jeremiah 51:33 .

corn of my floor. Literally son of my threshingfloor.

the LORD of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 .

the God of Israel. See note on Isaiah 29:23 .

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

entries.title: burden.
entries.content:
burden. The sixth of the seven burdens.

Dumah = Edom. An abbreviated form of fuller name "Idumea" (Isaiah 34:5 .Ezekiel 35:15 ; Ezekiel 36:5 .Mark 3:8; Mark 3:8 ).

Dumah = silence, prophetic of its end.

Seir. The inheritance of Esau (or Edom).

what of the night? = how far is it in the night? Note the Figure of speech Epizeuxis . Repeated in an abbreviated form thus: Hebrew. shomer mah-millayelah? shomer ma-milleyl ? = how far gone is the night? how far gone the night? This is Edom's inquiry.

entries.title: The morning cometh, &c.
entries.content:
The morning cometh, &c. This may be the oracle of silence implied in the name "Dumah" (see above, and compare Psalms 94:17 ; Psalms 115:17 ).

if ye will inquire. Isaiah had no answer. He is silent, but intimates that they may inquire again.

entries.title: burden.
entries.content:
burden. The seventh and last of the seven burdens

upon Arabia: ba'rab = in Arabia.

in Arabia: or, in the evening, or, at sunset. The name is as significant as "Dumah" (Isaiah 21:11 ).

travelling companies = caravans.

Dedanim = Dedanites, Descendants of Abraham by Keturah: Dedan, son of Midian (Genesis 25:3 . 1 Chronicles 1:32 ).

entries.title: Tema.
entries.content:
Tema. Descendants of Abraham through Hagar and Ishmael (Genesis 25:3 . 1 Chronicles 1:32 )

: both mentioned in Jeremiah 25:23 .Job 6:19 .

brought = bring ye.

prevented = meet ye.

entries.title: they fled.
entries.content: they fled. From the Assyrian invaders.

entries.title: Within a year.
entries.content:
Within a year. Later afflictions were foretold in Jeremiah 49:28 .

Kedar. Another descendant of Abraham by Hagar through Ishmael (Genesis 25:13 ).

entries.title: mighty men.
entries.content:
mighty men. Hebrew. gibbor . App-14 .

children = sons.

entries.title: burden
entries.content:
burden = oracle.

valley of vision. The Septuagint and Arabic versions render it Jerusalem, in relation to the high hills around. Similar names: "inhabitant of the valley, ""rock of the plain" (Jeremiah 21:13 ), "mountain in the fields" (Jeremiah 17:3 ). The reference is to Isaiah 22:5 .

vision. Here the most solemn visions had been seen: Abraham (Genesis 22:2 , Genesis 22:14 , compare the name Jehovah-jireh); also David (1 Chronicles 21:16 , 1 Chronicles 21:28 ). and the many visions of Isaiah (Isaiah 1:1 ; Isaiah 6:1-4 , &c). The Septuagint reads "Zion".

gone up, &c. Denoting a time of popular rejoicing. Refers to past time. Compare Matthew 24:16 . Luke 21:21 .

entries.title: stirs
entries.content: stirs = outcries. Referring to the time of this prophecy.

entries.title: from far
entries.content: from far = afar, or far away.

entries.title: Elam. Kir.
entries.content:
Elam. Kir. The south and north limits of the Chaldsean forces.

quiver. Hebrew. 'ashpah. Occurs only here in "former" portion, and only in Isaiah 49:2 in the "latter" portion.

chariots. See note on Isaiah 21:7 .

and. Some codices, with three early printed editions and Vulgate, read this "and "in the text.

entries.title: at
entries.content: at = toward.

entries.title: discovered
entries.content:
discovered = dismantled.

covering = veil.

entries.title: have seen
entries.content:
have seen = beheld.

the lower pool. The pool of Siloam. Compare Isa 7:3 ; 2 Chronicles 32:30 . The old pool. See notes on 2 Chronicles 32:3 , 2 Chronicles 32:30 , and App-68 .

entries.title: ditch
entries.content: ditch = a gathering of waters.

entries.title: let us, &c.
entries.content: let us, &c. Note Figure of speech Ellipsis ( App-6 ). Supply thus: "[saying, ] 'Let us eat', "&c. Compare 1 Corinthians 15:32 .

entries.title: the LORD of hosts.
entries.content:
the LORD of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 .

iniquity shall not be purged. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 30:10 . Leviticus 4:20 , &c). Compare Isaiah 6:7 ; Isaiah 27:9 ; and App-92 .

entries.title: Shebna.
entries.content:
Shebna. See 2 Kings 18:18 , 2 Kings 18:26 . Probably a foreigner, or heathenized Jew.

and say. Some codices, with Aramaean, Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate, read "and thou shalt say unto him".

entries.title: as he. rock
entries.content: as he. rock = (as. rock). Figure of speech Parenthesis.

entries.title: Behold.
entries.content:
Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos.

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, &c. = will hurl thee with the hurling of [a mighty] man.

entries.title: surely violently turn and toss thee.
entries.content: surely violently turn and toss thee. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia . Hebrew. zanoph, yiznaphka, zenephah.

entries.title: drive
entries.content:
drive = thrust.

station = office, or administration.

entries.title: in that day:
entries.content:
in that day: i.e. in the day when this prophecy will be fulfilled. Compare Isaiah 22:25 .

Eliakim = Whom God sets up. Hezekiah's minister. Probably superseded by Shebna in the evil days of Manasseh. See Isaiah 36:3 , Isaiah 36:22 ; Isaiah 37:2 .

entries.title: girdle.
entries.content:
girdle. Reference to Pentateuch. Occurs here; and elsewhere only in Exodus 28:4 , Exodus 28:39 , Exodus 28:40 ; Exodus 29:9 ; Exodus 39:29 . Leviticus 8:7 , Leviticus 8:13 ; Leviticus 16:4 . App-92 . A priestly vestment.

government = administration.

entries.title: so
entries.content:
so = and.

open and. shut. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for power of administration. Compare Revelation 3:7 , which shows that the fulfilment culminates in Messiah.

entries.title: the offspring and the issue:
entries.content:
the offspring and the issue: i.e. direct and collateral issue, and embraces his entire kindred.

the offspring. Hebrew. hazze'eza'im. Occurs only in Job and Isaiah (Job 5:25 ; Job 21:8 ; Job 27:14 ; Job 31:8 , and Isaiah 34:1 ; Isaiah 42:5 ; Isaiah 44:3 ; Isaiah 48:19 ; Isaiah 61:9 ; Isaiah 65:23 ). See App-79 .

vessels. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject), App-6 , for the kindred mentioned above.

entries.title: In that day.
entries.content:
In that day. Refers back to the day of Isaiah 22:20 , i.e. the day of Shebna's overthrow. This would be the day of Eliakim's exaltation.

the nail: which Shebna thought himself to be, but which Jehovah declared Eliakim to be.

removed. cut down. fall. cut off. Referring to verses: Isaiah 22:17-19 . Figure of speech Synonymia , emphasizing the completeness of Shebna's downfall. The interpretation belongs to the two men, but the application refers (1) to the two parties in Jerusalem, and (2) to the Messiah, in Whom the prophecy will be exhausted.

entries.title: burden
entries.content:
burden = oracle.

Tyre. It had rejoiced in the misfortunes of Judah (Amos 1:9 ); so it is punished by the same king of Babylon (Isaiah 23:13 ). Ezekiel 26:2-21 .

Ships of Tarshish. See note on Isaiah 2:16 and 1 Kings 10:22 .

ships. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the people in them.

house. In this case "port".

Chittim. Originally used of Cyprus, but extended to the islands and coast-lands of the Mediterranean.

it: i.e. the fall of Tyre.

entries.title: isle.
entries.content:
isle. Here, Tyre itself.

thou whom = which.

pass over = cross, in trading. In verses: Isaiah 23:2 , Isaiah 23:3 , Isaiah 23:6 , Isaiah 23:10 , Isaiah 23:12 , imperative, implying flight.

entries.title: seed:
entries.content:
seed: or, grain.

Sihor = the black river, the Nile (compare Jeremiah 2:18 ).

harvest. Egypt was the field, the Phoenician coast its granary.

river. Reference to Pentateuch. See note on Isaiah 7:18 . "River" is here put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the country (Egypt) through which it passes.

she is a mart of nations: or, it became merchandise for the nations.

mart = gain resulting from merchandise, as in Isaiah 23:18 (Isaiah 45:14 .Proverbs 3:14 ; Proverbs 31:18 ).

entries.title: Zidon.
entries.content:
Zidon. Was a seaport. the mother city of Phoenicia, the granary of Egypt's harvests. The Zidonians had built Tyre on a rocky island, and connected it with the mainland.

I travail not = I have not travailed. The verbs which follow in Isaiah 23:4 are in the past tense. The sea speaks to the mother Zidon: thou seekest Tyre thou findest only the sea.

children = sons.

entries.title: As at the report concerning &c.
entries.content: As at the report concerning &c. : or, When the report comes to Egypt they are forthwith in terror at the report concerning Tyre.

entries.title: antiquity
entries.content:
antiquity = origin.

feet. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject), for the vessels in which the Tyrians fled from Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.title: crowning
entries.content: crowning = crown-giver: i.e. conferring crowns on other Phoenician cities.

entries.title: The Lord of hosts.
entries.content:
The Lord of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 .

stain = pollute.

entries.title: the Lord.
entries.content:
the Lord. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

the merchant city = Tyre, or Phoenician coast. Hosea 12:7 .

thereof: or, which are upon it.

entries.title: oppressed
entries.content: oppressed = humbled.

entries.title: this people was not
entries.content:
this people was not = a people that were no people (i.e. Assyria). Tyre boasted antiquity (Isaiah 23:7 ), Assyria was their object-lesson and warning.

and: or, but.

He. God.

entries.title: seventy years.
entries.content:
seventy years. See Jeremiah 25:9-11 ; Jeremiah 27:2-7 . From the first year of Nebuchadnezzar (496 B.C.) to the conquest of Babylon by Cyrus (426 B.C.)

one. Hebrew. ehad , a compound unity, hence "one" of a dynasty, here, the Babylonian dynasty. Not yahid , a single one. See note on Deuteronomy 6:4 .

entries.title: Take an harp, &c.
entries.content: Take an harp, &c. Figure of speech Apostrophe . Not a quotation.

entries.title: world
entries.content:
world = the earth. Hebrew. ha- arez .

upon = which are upon.

earth = ground, or, soil. Hebrew. ha- adamah .

entries.title: holiness
entries.content:
holiness = hallowed.

sufficiently = abundantly.

entries.title: Behold.
entries.content:
Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos .

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

earth. Hebrew ha- 'arez . Occurs sixteen times in this chapter. Rendered "land" in verses: Isaiah 24:3 , Isaiah 24:11 , Isaiah 24:13

empty . Note the Figure of speech Synonymia , "empty", "waste", "upside down", "scattered abroad". See App-6 .

entries.title: as . . . so.
entries.content:
as . . . so. Figure of speech Simile .

the lender . . . the borrower. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 22:25 , Exodus 22:27 . Deuteronomy 15:2 ; Deuteronomy 24:10 , Deuteronomy 24:11 ). See App-92 .

entries.title: The land:
entries.content:
The land: Hebrew. ha-'drez , as in Isaiah 24:1 .

utterly emptied. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia , for emphasis. Hebrew. hibb6k tibbdk .

utterly spoiled. Hebrew. hibb6z tibboz .

entries.title: mourneth.
entries.content:
mourneth. See note on Isaiah 3:26 .

mourneth and fadeth away. languish. Hebrew. umlelah nablah tebel umlalu .

the earth, &c. Figure of speech Prosopopoeia . This is one of the three places where (in the Hebrew) one verse ends with "the earth" and the next verse begins with "the earth", being the Figure of speech Anadiplosis . The other two passages are Genesis 1:1 , Genesis 1:2 , and Hosea 2:23 , Hos 2:24 .

entries.title: The earth.
entries.content:
The earth. See last note on p. 959.

transgressed. Hebrew. 'abar . App-44 .

the laws. the everlasting covenant. Reference to Pentateuch. See note on Genesis 9:16 ; and App-92 , The Pentateuch was as well known to Isaiah as to the kings in whose reigns he prophesied.

entries.title: Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth.
entries.content:
Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth. Some codices, with four early printed editions (one in margin), and Syriac, read "Because of a curse the earth mourneth".

earth. Hebrew. 'erez .

desolate = laid waste. Hebrew. 'asham. Compare verses: Isaiah 24:10 , Isaiah 24:12 , Isaiah 24:23 .

entries.title: new wine
entries.content: new wine = must. Hebrew. tirosh . App-27 .

entries.title: tabrets
entries.content: tabrets = drums. See note on drums, 1 Samuel 10:5 .

entries.title: wine.
entries.content:
wine. Hebrew. yayin . App-27 .

strong drink. Hebrew. shekar App-27 .

entries.title: confusion
entries.content:
confusion = desolation. Hebrew. tohu . Same word as "without form". Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 1:2 ). Occurs in "former" portion three times (here; Isaiah 29:1 , "thing of naught; "Isaiah 34:11 ); and in the "latter" portion eight times (Isaiah 40:17 , Isaiah 40:23 ; Isaiah 41:29 ; Isaiah 44:9 , "vanity; "Isaiah 45:18 , Isaiah 45:19 , "in vain; "Isaiah 49:4 , "naught; "Isaiah 59:4 , "vanity").

no man = no one.

entries.title: desolation
entries.content: desolation = astonishment. Hebrew. shamen . Compare Isaiah 24:6 , Isaiah 24:10 , Isaiah 24:23 .

entries.title: sea.
entries.content: sea. Note the Figure of speech Ellipsis = sea [saying]. See note on Psalms 109:5 .

entries.title: fires:
entries.content:
fires: Or, valleys.

isles = maritime countries. See note on Isaiah 11:1 .

entries.title: the righteous
entries.content:
the righteous = the righteous One (singular): i.e. the One referred to in Isaiah 24:15 ; or, the nation, as in Isaiah 26:2 . compare Acts 3:14 ; Acts 7:52 ; Acts 22:14 .

I said = I had said: i. e the land. Figure of speech Prosopopaeia .

My leanness, my leanness. Figure of speech Epizeuxis , for emphasis.

treacherous dealers, &c. = traitors have betrayed.

entries.title: Fear, and the pit, and the snare.
entries.content: Fear, and the pit, and the snare. Figure of speech Synonymia , and Figure of speech Paonomasia , not a "play on words", but for great and solemn emphasis. Hebrew. paphad , vapahath, happa vappaph (tr. Eng., scare, lair, snare).

entries.title: fear. pit. snare.
entries.content:
fear. pit. snare. Figure of speech Paronomasia

again. Hebrew. happahad. huppahath. happahath bapah . See Luke 21:35 , and compare Jeremiah 48:43 , Jeremiah 48:44 .

the windows from on high, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 7:11 ).

are open = have opened.

foundations of the earth. See Isaiah 58:12 . Compare Isaiah 40:21 .

entries.title: utterly broken down.
entries.content:
utterly broken down. Note Figure of speech Polyptoton . Hebrew breaking, breaks up. Same Figure of speech below.

clean dissolved. Hebrew bursting, bursts up.

moved exceedingly. Hebrew tottering, tottereth.

entries.title: reel to and fro.
entries.content:
reel to and fro. Hebrew staggering, staggereth.

removed. Hebrew rocketh to and fro.

transgression = revolt. Hebrew. pasha . App-44 . Not the same word as in Isaiah 24:5 .

entries.title: that are.
entries.content:
that are. Omit.

earth = the ground, or, Soil. Hebrew. ha-adamah . Compare Isaiah 6:12 .

entries.title: pit.
entries.content:
pit. Not the same word as in verses: Isaiah 24:17 , Isaiah 24:18 . Here, Hebrew. bor , a dug-out pit, or dungeon. Occurs in Isaiah 14:15 , Isaiah 14:19 ; Isaiah 36:13 ; Isaiah 38:18 ; and in "latter" portion, Isaiah 51:1 . App-79 .

and = even.

visited: i.e. with the judgments foretold in the preceding Verses. Compare Isaiah 10:3 ; Isaiah 26:14 , Isaiah 26:16 ; Isaiah 29:6 .

entries.title: confounded
entries.content:
confounded = blush (from shame).

ashamed = turn pale (from fear).

the LORD of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 .

ancients = elders. Compare Revelation 4:4 .

gloriously = in glory, or "[shall be] a glory".

entries.title: I will exalt Thee, I will praise Thy name.
entries.content:
I will exalt Thee, I will praise Thy name. In Hebrew three words, two making the Figure of speech Paronomasia ( App-6 ); not for a "play on words", but for solemn emphasis, to attract our attention. Hebrew. 'aromimka , 'odeh shimka . Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 15:2 ). App-92 .

wonderful things = a wonderful deed.

entries.title: strangers
entries.content: strangers = foreigners. See note on Isaiah 5:17 .

entries.title: strength
entries.content:
strength = stronghold.

poor. Hebrew. dal = impoverished, reduced. See note on "poverty" Proverbs 6:11 .

when the blast of the terrible ones is = for the blast of the terrible ones [is], &c.

blast. Hebrew. ruach ( App-9 ), as in Isaiah 37:7 . Exodus 15:8 . 2 Kings 19:7 . branch = triumphal song.

brought low = become low.

entries.title: the LORD of hosts.
entries.content:
the LORD of hosts. See note on 1 Samuel 1:3 .

people = the peoples.

a feast. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia in this verse: a feast (Hebrew. mishteh) of fat things (Hebrew. shemanim) , a feast of (Hebrew. mishteh) wines on the lees (Hebrew. shemarim) ; of fat things (Hebrew. shemanim)

full of marrow (Hebrew. memuhyim) , of wines on the lees (Hebrew. shemarim) . All these words are thus heaped together to impress us with the greatness of this feast.

wines on the lees. Hebrew. shemarim ( App-27 ), see above = wines purified from the lees.

entries.title: destroy
entries.content:
destroy = swallow up, as in Isaiah 25:8 .

this mountain: i.e. Zion (Isaiah 2:1 , Isaiah 2:2 ; Isaiah 24:23 ).

cast = covered.

people = the peoples.

entries.title: swallow up.
entries.content:
swallow up. Same word as "destroy" (Isaiah 25:7 ), so as to cause a thing to disappear and be no more. Compare Numbers 16:30 . Psalms 69:15 ; Psalms 106:17 . Jonah 1:17 .

in victory. Hebrew. nezah = for ever. Occurs in Isaiah 13:20 ; Isaiah 28:28 ; Isaiah 33:20 ; Isaiah 34:10 ; and in the "latter portion", Isaiah 57:16 ; rendered "victory" in 1 Chronicles 29:11 . 1 Samuel 15:29 . Quoted in 1 Corinthians 15:54

: where we have the Holy Spirit's comment on the word, giving the additional thought of "victory". See App-79 .

rebuke = reproach.

entries.title: we have waited.
entries.content: we have waited. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 49:18 .)

entries.title: Moab. as straw. for the dunghill.
entries.content:
Moab. as straw. for the dunghill. Note the Figure of speech Homoeopropheron ( App-6 ). Moab. mathben , beMo Madmenah . which occurs only here, is used to complete the Figure of speech Homoeopropheron . See above.

trodden down = beaten to pieces by treading.

for the dunghill = in Madmenah, as in Isaiah 10:31 and Jeremiah 48:2 , Revised Version quite wrong, "in the water of the dunghill". Dung is never watered in the East, but dried, and used as fuel (Ezekiel 4:15 ), and is found only in the streets of towns and villages. In Psalms 83:10 "earth" is adamah = ground. See note there.

entries.title: spread forth His hands.
entries.content:
spread forth His hands. In the East all swimmers swim "hand over hand", and beat the water with loud noise. Parallel with the beating of straw in Isaiah 25:10 . Compare Isaiah 63 .

as=according as.

spoils = devices, or artifices.

entries.title: bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground.
entries.content: bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground. Note the Figure of speech Synonymia , to emphasize the certainty and reality of what had been expressed by the Figure of speech Simile in verses: Isaiah 25:10 , Isaiah 25:11 .

entries.title: In that day:
entries.content:
In that day: i.e. in the yet future day, when these judgments shall have been accomplished.

Judah. In Isaiah 2 6 we have the Song of Judah (Isaiah 26:1 ); in Isaiah 27 , the Song of Israel. Compare verses: Isaiah 26:6 , Isaiah 26:12 .

entries.title: keepeth the truth
entries.content: keepeth the truth = maintaineth fidelity. No Article. Compare Deuteronomy 32:20 . Occurs only here, in Isaiah.

entries.title: perfect peace.
entries.content:
perfect peace. Hebrew peace, peace. Figure of speech Epizeuxis , for emphasis, beautifully expressed In the Authorized Version. The same expression occurs in Isaiah 57:19 , indicating the unity of the book. See note on Isaiah 24:16 , and App-79 . Compare Isaiah 27:5 .

mind = thought.

trusteth = confideth. Hebrew. batah . See App-69 .

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

THE LORD. Hebrew Jah. App-4 . In Isaiah, only here and Isaiah 12:2 ; Isaiah 38:11 , Isaiah 38:11 .

JEHOVAH. One of the four passages where the Authorized Version transliterates the word instead of translating it. See note on Isaiah 12:2 , and App-48 .

everlasting strength = a rock of ages. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 32:4 , Deuteronomy 32:18 , Deuteronomy 32:30 , same word as here). See App-92 . Found only in Deuteronomy and as applied to God (see App-79 ); and here, and Isaiah 30:29 , in the "former" portion; and Isaiah 44:8 in the "latter" portion. Compare Habakkuk 1:12 .

1 Samuel 2:2 . 2 Samuel 23:3 , and Psalms.

entries.title: bringeth down, &c.
entries.content:
bringeth down, &c. See note on Isaiah 25:12 .

ground = earth. Hebrew ' erez .

entries.title: poor
entries.content:
poor = wretched, afflicted. Here singular. Hebrew. amah . See note on Proverbs 6:11 .

needy = lowly ones.

entries.title: way.
entries.content:
way. See note on "path", Isaiah 2:3 .

the just = a just one.

uprightness = a perfect or level way.

weigh = ponder.

entries.title: we waited.
entries.content:
we waited. See note on Isaiah 25:9 .

soul. Hebrew. nephesh . App-13 .

remembrance. Reference to Pentateuch. Same as "memorial" in Exodus 3:15 . The words are quoted again in Psalms 102:12 ; Psalms 135:13 and Hosea 12:5 , and nowhere else. App-92 .

entries.title: spirit.
entries.content:
spirit. Hebrew. ruach . App-9 .

early = with the dawn.

when, &c. Hence the multitudes which come out of the great tribulation in Revelation 7:14-17 .

entries.title: the wicked
entries.content: the wicked = a lawless one. Hebrew. rasha . App-44 .

entries.title: the fire, &c.
entries.content: the fire, &c. or, fire shall devour Thine adversaries (Revised Version)

entries.title: ordain
entries.content:
ordain = arrange.

in us = for us. Compare Philippians 1:2 , Philippians 1:13 . App-4 .

lords = owners. Referring to the Canaanite oppressors of Israel and their false gods.

had dominion = domineered, or lorded it.

make mention = call upon.

Thy name = Thee. See note on Psalms 20:1 .

entries.title: They are dead:
entries.content:
They are dead: i.e. the "other lords" of Isaiah 26:13 . Hebrew. methim . Not dead men, as such, for "all" men shall rise again (2 John 1:5; 2 John 1:5 :28 , John 5:29 . Acts 23:6 , Acts 23:8 ; Acts 24:15 . 1 Corinthians 15:22 .Revelation 20:4-6 , Revelation 20:13 ), but those referred to in Isaiah 26:13 .

deceased = the Rephaim . This is a proper name, and should not be translated. Where it is translated it is always rendered "giants" or "dead" (Isaiah 26:19 . Job 26:5 .Psalms 88:10 . Proverbs 2:18 ; Proverbs 9:18 ; Proverbs 21:16 . Proverbs 14:9 ); why not so here? or transliterated, as it is in Isaiah 17:5 .

they shall not rise. These Rephaim will not rise. They were the progeny of the fallen angels: these latter are kept "in prison" (1 Peter 3:19 ), in "chains" (2 Peter 2:4 .Jude 1:6; Jude 1:6 ), "reserved" unto judgment: but their progeny will "not rise"(verses: Isaiah 26:14 , Isaiah 26:19 ) or be judged, for they have been "visited", "destroyed", and:'perished". See App-23 and App-25 .

entries.title: the nation:
entries.content: the nation: i.e. Israel. The future nation of Matthew 21:43 .

entries.title: Like as a woman. &c.
entries.content: Like as a woman. &c. These refer to the birth-pangs of the Great Tribulation, which issue in the new nation.

entries.title: neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen
entries.content:
neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen = nor did the inhabitants of the world come to the light: i.e. by being born. The Hebrew naphal, to fall, is used of birth, as Hebrew. nephel occurs only in Job 3:16 . Psalms 58:8 . Ecclesiastes 6:3 .

world = the inhabited world. Hebrew. tebel.

entries.title: Thy dead men
entries.content:
Thy dead men = Thy dead ones. Hebrew. methim, as in Isaiah 26:14 . These are very different from the dead in Isaiah 26:14 . They are Jehovah's dead. These shall rise.

my dead body shall. arise = my corpse (a noun of multitude).

shall they arise (plural verb): i.e. all the dead bodies of Jehovah's people. All these shall awake and sing (Psalms 17:15 ).

dwell in dust = lie in the dust: i.e. buried in the dust of the earth.

as the dew of herbs = like the dew upon herbs: i.e. revivifying them. Compare Isaiah 66:14 .

and = but; introducing the important contrast already expressed in Isaiah 26:14 .

cast ou t: or, cast away. Not yield up in resurrection. Whom will the earth thus cast away? See the answer in the word which follows.

the dead = the Rephaim. See note on Isaiah 26:14 , and App-23 and App-25 . These will "not rise".

entries.title: Come
entries.content: Come = Go.

entries.title: disclose her blood.
entries.content: disclose her blood. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 4:10 , Genesis 4:11 ).

entries.title: In that day:
entries.content:
In that day: i.e. the period of judgment foretold in Isaiah 26:21 .

leviathan. Three great aquatic animals are here mentioned: probably referring to Israel's three great enemies: Assyria (with Nineveh, on the Tigris); Babylon (on the Euphrates); and Egypt (on the Nile); with Satan himself behind them all, as their great instigator.

piercing = fleeing, or fugitive (like the Tigris). crooked tortuous (like the winding Euphrates).

dragon = the crocodile of the Nile.

sea = the Nile, as in Isaiah 19:5 .Nahum 3:8 .

entries.title: sing:
entries.content:
sing: or, answer.

red wine. Hebrew. chemer. App-27 . Some codices, with one early printed edition, Aramaean, and Septuagint, read chemed, pleasant, or lovely.

entries.title: Fury.
entries.content:
Fury. Hebrew. chemah = heat, wrath, displeasure.

not in Me: i.e. not now. There was in the other song (Isaiah 5:5-7 ): but now, "in that day", all wrath will have gone.

briers and thorns: i.e. the internal enemies of the vineyard (as the wild beasts are the external enemies). These are now the objects of His wrath, not His vineyard.

entries.title: Or:
entries.content:
Or: i.e. if such enemies wish to avert My wrath, let them make peace with Me.

My strength = Me, as a refuge or protection.

entries.title: He shall cause, &c.
entries.content:
He shall cause, &c. This verse is not an "addendum". or "irrelevant", or "an illegible gap". It is necessary in order to give us the subject of the song, which is reserved till this verse. The symbol is to tell us that Israel is the vineyard (Compare Isaiah 27:12 ). See the Structure on the previous page; and note that in (Isaiah 26:1-21 ) we have the Song of Judah, while in (Isaiah 27:2-6 ) the song concerning Israel.

the world = the inhabited world. Hebrew. tebel.

entries.title: as, &c.
entries.content: as, &c. = according to the stroke of those, &c.

entries.title: In measure
entries.content:
In measure = By measure. Referring to the smiting of Israel, as being in limited measure. Hebrew. seah . App-51 . (11), (5).

when it shooteth forth = when Thou didst send it forth (i.e. the stroke of Isaiah 27:7 ).

Thou wilt debate with it = Thou wilt curb it (i.e. the stroke of Isaiah 27:7 ). Hebrew. rib . = plead, as in Isaiah 1:17 ; Isaiah 3:13 ; Isaiah 51:22 .Jeremiah 2:9 , Jeremiah 2:29 ; Jeremiah 12:1 ; Jeremiah 50:34 .Micah 7:9 .

rough = harsh, or severe.

wind. Hebrew. ruach . App-9 .

east wind. A violent, hot, scorching wind; pernicious to the fruit of a vineyard.

entries.title: By this
entries.content:
By this = In this way.

iniquity. Hebrew. avah . App-44 .

purged = covered: i.e. atoned for. Hebrew. kaphar . See note on Exodus 29:33 .

this is all the fruit = all this is the fruit or result.

sin. Hebrew. chata '. App-44 .

the altar = [all] altars.

as = no better than.

in sunder = to pieces.

the groves = the Asherahs. App-42 .

images = images of Ashtoreth. See note on Isaiah 17:8 .

not = no more.

entries.title: Yet
entries.content:
Yet = For.

forsaken. See note on Isaiah 1:4 .

consume = devour.

entries.title: the boughs, &c.
entries.content:
the boughs, &c. = her harvest drieth up.

they. Feminine., i.e. the "stones" of Isaiah 27:9 .

broken off = broken, or destroyed.

entries.title: in that day:
entries.content:
in that day: verses: Isaiah 27:12 , Isaiah 27:13 refer to Israel, as verses: Isaiah 27:7 , Isaiah 27:10-11 refer to Israel's enemies.

beat off: i.e. as olives from a tree = "beat off [his fruit]": i.e. gather the sons of Israel.

channel = flood.

river: i.e. the Euphrates.

children = sons.

entries.title: ready to perish.
entries.content:
ready to perish. So the end will be like the beginning. See Deuteronomy 26:5 .

holy. See note on Exodus 3:5 .

mount = mountain.

hasty fruit = early fig [becomes].

eateth it up = swalloweth it.

entries.title: Woe
entries.content:
Woe = Ho! We now come to a cycle of woes corresponding with the "burdens". In these "woes" Jehovah's purpose is alternately thrown into sharp contrast (see the Structure, above). crown of pride = pride's crown, or proud crown (i.e. Samaria; compare Amos 6:1 , Amos 6:3 ). Figure of speech Enallage ( App-6 ). Referring to the circle of towers which girdled Samaria.

to = of.

Ephraim = one tribe. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for all the tribes of Israel.

a fading flower. Compare Isaiah 1:30 ; Isaiah 40:7 .

fat = rich, or luxuriant.

entries.title: hath a mighty and strong one
entries.content:
hath a mighty and strong one = hath a mighty one, immensely strong: i.e. Assyria (2 Kings 17:5 , 2 Kings 17:6 ).

cast down = cast [Ephraim] down.

entries.title: be
entries.content:
be = become.

and. Omit.

hasty fruit = early fig [becomes].

eateth it up = swalloweth it.

entries.title: the Lord of hosts.
entries.content: the Lord of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 .

entries.title: spirit.
entries.content:
spirit. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

turn = turn, or drive, back.

entries.title: they.
entries.content:
they. Referring to Judah.

strong drink. Hebrew. shekar . App-27 .

judgment = pronouncing judgment.

entries.title: tabled.
entries.content: tabled. Used at sacrificial feasts (Tabernacles, Harvest, &c.) 1 Samuel 20:34 .Ezekiel 40:39-43 .Malachi 1:7 , Malachi 1:12 .

entries.title: Whom
entries.content:
Whom = Whom [say they].

milk. breasts? (Two questions.)

entries.title: For
entries.content:
For = For [say they] mimicking the prophet as though he were teaching little children in a school.

must be: or, [hath been]. The verse then reads: "For it is zav lazav, zav lazav kav lakav, kav lakav ze'er sham, ze'er sham . "The Figures of speech: Epizeuxis and Paronomasia ( App-6 ), for emphasis. It may be Englished by: "Law upon law, Saw upon saw".

entries.title: For
entries.content:
For = Yea, verily. Taking the words out of their own taunting lips, and turning them against themselves. Quoted in 1 Corinthians 14:21 .

stammering = jabbering.

another = foreign. Referring to the Assyrian language they were (alas!) soon to hear (Compare Isaiah 33:19 . Deuteronomy 28:49 ).

He speak: i.e. by the Assyrians.

entries.title: To whom He said:
entries.content: To whom He said: or, He (Jehovah) Who said to them: i.e. by His prophets (Isaiah 7:4 ; Isaiah 8:6 ; Isaiah 30:15 ).

entries.title: was
entries.content:
was = became. Giving back to the scoffers their own words (from Isaiah 28:10 ) in the form of a threatening.

might = may.

fall backward, &c. Note the Figure of speech Synonymia , by which the similar words are heaped together to impress on them the solemnity and certainty of the judgment.

taken = caught.

entries.title: made
entries.content:
made = cut, or solemnized.

made a covenant. It is alleged that the use of the word "covenant" is confined to Jehovah by the "second Isaiah" (i.e. after Isaiah 40 ): but it is so used before that (See Isaiah 24:5 ; Isaiah 33:8 ), But why should not a covenant be made with, and by, other parties as it is here in Isaiah 28:15 , Isaiah 28:18 ? See App-79 .

hell. Hebrew Sheol. App-35 .

entries.title: I lay
entries.content:
I lay = I have laid. So the Syriac and Septuagint. Laid, in the counsels of eternity: in Abraham's promise (Genesis 12 ); in David's covenant (2 Samuel 7 ).

in Zion. In Zion; not Zion itself.

a stone. This is a distinct reference to Isaiah 49:24 . It is the Immanuel (of Isaiah 7 ), the promised Son (of Isaiah 9 ), the rod from Jesse's stem (of Isaiah 11 ).

a tried stone = a test stone: i.e. tested itself, and testing others. Compare Isaiah 28:17 , and Zechariah 3:9 .

a sure foundation. Figure of speech Polyptoton ( App-6 ), for emphasis. Hebrew a foundation founded: i.e. a wellfounded foundation, or a firm or sure foundation.

not make haste = be constant, steady, not fleeing away. See note on Proverbs 8:30 . Note the Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject), by which the hastening, or flight is put for the confusion and shame which is the cause of it. Septuagint reads "ashamed". In Romans 9:33 ; Romans 10:11 . 1 Peter 2:6 , the Figure of speech is translated, and means therefore exactly the same thing: = shall have no need for hurried flight (Compare Isaiah 49:23 ).

entries.title: Judgment also will I lay to the line, &c.
entries.content: Judgment also will I lay to the line, &c. = I will make judgment the line, and righteousness the plumbline.

entries.title: take you
entries.content:
take you = take you away.

vexation = terror.

report = hearing. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for what is heard.

entries.title: the bed, &c.
entries.content: the bed, &c. This allegory is to show that their false security as to the approach of Sennacherib would afford them no real rest, it would soon be disturbed.

entries.title: Perazim. Gibeon.
entries.content:
Perazim. Gibeon. This could not be known or understood without reference to 2 Samuel 5:20 , and Joshua 10:10 ; and this reference must have been in writing: too long before (700 years) to be a matter of mere memory. See App-92 .

His strange work = strange His work [is]. Hebrew. zur = foreign.

His strange act = unwonted [is] His act. Hebrew. nakar.

entries.title: earth
entries.content: earth = land, or soil.

entries.title: plow all day:
entries.content:
plow all day: i.e. continually = ever keep ploughing? See the note on Isaiah 28:28 .

he open = he [for ever] open.

entries.title: The principal wheat
entries.content: The principal wheat = wheat in rows. Only here. place = due order. Connect "appointed" with "place", not with "barley".

entries.title: For his God, &c.
entries.content:
For his God, &c. Render: "For One hath instructed him in the right course; his God doth teach him".

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

entries.title: threshing instrument.
entries.content: threshing instrument. Only here, and Isaiah 41:15 .

entries.title: Bread
entries.content:
Bread = Corn. Bread is put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Effect), for the corn of which it is made. Compare Job 28:5 .

bruised = crushed: i.e. reduced to powder. Compare Exodus 32:20 . 2 Kings 23:6 . Render, as a question: Is corn crushed? because = nay. The Hebrew accent t ebir is disjunctive and requires this rendering. Compare Revised Version margin, and Job 22:2 .

ever = for ever.

entries.title: This:
entries.content:
This: i.e. this same design in His treatment of His people. His purpose is the same as that of the husbandman. Compare Amos 9:9 .

excellent = lofty.

working = wisdom. The sort of wisdom which carries the purpose through to permanency. Hebrew. tushiyah, See note on Proverbs 2:7 .

entries.title: Woe.
entries.content:
Woe. The second of the six woes.

Ariel = either a lion of GOD (El, App-4 . IV) (2 Samuel 23:20 ); or the altar-hearth of GOD (Ezekiel 43:15 , Ezekiel 43:16 ; and the Moabite Stone, line 12, App-54 ). Jerusalem is called Har-el on old Egyptian monuments.

the city. Put by Figure of speech Polyonymia for Jerusalem. "City" is in the construct state: = city of [the spot] where David camped.

dwelt = encamped.

year. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for festival.

let them kill, &c.: or, let the feasts go round. Figure of speech Eironeia. App-6 .

entries.title: as Ariel
entries.content: as Ariel = as a veritable hearth of GOD.

entries.title: ground
entries.content:
ground =. earth. a familiar spirit = an Ob . See note on Leviticus 19:31 .

whisper = peep, chirp, or mutter.

entries.title: strangers:
entries.content:
strangers: i.e. adversaries.

like, &c. . . . as, &c. Figure of speech Hyperbole.

terrible ones = tyrants.

entries.title: visited.
entries.content:
visited. These judgments (in Isaiah 29:6 ) refer to the deliverance from Jerusalem's enemies.

the LORD of hosts. See note on 1 Samuel 1:3 .

entries.title: Ariel.
entries.content: Ariel. Here it is plainly Jerusalem.

entries.title: as
entries.content:
as = according as.

soul. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

entries.title: wine.
entries.content:
wine. Hebrew. yayin. App-27 .

strong drink. Hebrew. shekar. App-27 .

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

hath poured, &c. Quoted in Romans 11:8 .

spirit. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

entries.title: of all
entries.content:
of all = of the whole, or altogether.

book = scroll, or document, in writing.

entries.title: the LORD*.
entries.content:
the LORD*. One of the 134 places where the Sopherim say they changed Jehovah of the primitive text to Adonai. See App-32 .

said. Quoted in Matthew 15:7-9 . Mark 7:6 .

but = though.

taught by the precept of men = a commandment of men in which they have been schooled: i.e. taught by rote.

men = mortals. Hebrew, plural of enosh . App-14 .

entries.title: for.
entries.content:
for. Quoted in 1 Corinthians 1:19 .

wisdom. Hebrew. chakam. See notes on

understanding. Hebrew. binah. Proverbs 1:2 .

entries.title: say.
entries.content: say. Compare Isaiah 45:9 .

entries.title: book
entries.content: book = scroll.

entries.title: meek
entries.content:
meek = oppressed.

poor = oppressed. Hebrew. 'ebyon. See note on Proverbs 6:11 .

the Holy One of Israel. See note on Isaiah 1:4 .

entries.title: the terrible one
entries.content: the terrible one = the tyrant.

entries.title: make a man an offender for a word
entries.content:
make a man an offender for a word = who bring a man into condemnation by a word (i.e. by false witness).

reproveth = decideth: i.e. in judgment.

just = righteous.

a thing of nought. See note on "confusion", Isaiah 24:10 .

entries.title: Abraham.
entries.content:
Abraham. Reference to Pentateuch, as well known. App-92 .

the house of Jacob. See note on Isaiah 2:5 .

his face . . . wax pale. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for fear.

entries.title: children
entries.content:
children = young children.

the God of Israel. This expression occurs seven times in Isaiah (here; Isaiah 41:17 ; Isaiah 45:3 , Isaiah 45:15 ; Isaiah 48:1 , Isaiah 48:2 ; Isaiah 52:12 ). Elsewhere twenty-nine times, without Jehovah preceding (Genesis 33:20 . Exodus 24:10 . Numbers 16:9 . Joshua 22:16 . 1Sa 1:17 ; 1 Samuel 5:7 , 1Sa 5:8 , 1 Samuel 5:8 , 1Sa 5:8 , 1 Samuel 5:10 , 1 Samuel 5:11 ; 1Sa 6:3 , 1 Samuel 6:5 ; 1 Samuel 25:32 . 2 Samuel 23:3 .Ezra 3:2 , &c.

entries.title: shall come, &c.
entries.content: shall come, &c. = shall know discernment.

entries.title: Woe.
entries.content:
Woe. The third of the six woes.

rebellious = stubborn, or backsliding.

children = sons.

take counsel = carry out a purpose. cover with a covering: or, pour out a libation; and so, make an alliance.

My Spirit = Me. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

entries.title: walk
entries.content:
walk = are setting out. This prophecy had been given in the days of Hezekiah (617-588), and was then being fulfilled in Israel. strength of Pharaoh. Compare Isaiah 30:7 , where it is shown to be a vain help. In verses: Isaiah 30:2 , Isaiah 30:3 , "strength" is literal. In Isaiah 30:7 it is a Figure.

trust = flee for refuge to. Hebrew. hasah. App-69 . Same word as in Isaiah 30:3 , but not the same as in Isaiah 30:12 .

entries.title: his:
entries.content:
his: i.e. Pharaoh's.

Zoan. Now Zan.

learn doctrine = accept instruction. Hanes. Called Tahapanes (Jeremiah 2:16 ). Now Tell Defenneh , about seventy miles from Cairo, the capital of a minor district. Succeeding Memphis as the capital before Abraham's time. Known to the Greeks as Hiracleopolis Magna. The name occurs only in Scripture.

entries.title: burden.
entries.content:
burden. Refers to the lading of the animals of the ambassadors who were going down to Egypt with rich gifts to secure an alliance, and thus reversing the steps of their national deliverance. It is not a fresh "burden", "the beginning of which has been lost".

the south = the Negeb, which must be passed through to get to Egypt. See notes on Genesis 13:1 , and Psalms 126:4 .

the viper, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 8:15 ). Occurs in Isaiah only here, and in Isaiah 59:5 . App-92 .

riches. Hebrew. hayil = strength. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the riches or treasures carried by it.

to = [relying] upon: i.e. the Egyptians, as stated in preceding clause.

entries.title: have I cried concerning this
entries.content:
have I cried concerning this = have I called (or named) her.

Their strength, &c. Hebrew Egypt sitting still (and thus not giving the help that was being sought). Rahab = pride, or strength, is put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for Egypt, the proud or strong one. Note the wrong but common use of this verse, through not heeding the context.

entries.title: a table
entries.content:
a table = a tablet.

note = inscribe. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 17:14 ; Exodus 24:4 .

the time to come = the latter day.

entries.title: children
entries.content:
children = sons.

law: or, instruction contained in the law of Moses, See note on Isaiah 1:10 .

entries.title: trust
entries.content: trust = confide. Hebrew. b a t ah ( App-69 .) Not the same word as in verses: Isaiah 30:2 , Isaiah 30:3 . Same as in Isaiah 30:15 .

entries.title: as the breaking of the potters' vessel.
entries.content:
as the breaking of the potters' vessel. The reference is to the manufacture of homrah, by breaking up pottery to powder in order to make cement of it. Carried on in the valley of Hinnom. See note on Jeremiah 19:1 , Jeremiah 19:2 .

fire from the hearth = that which is kindled.

pit = cistern.

entries.title: confidence
entries.content:
confidence = trust: i.e. trust [in Jehovah]. Hebrew. batah , as in Isaiah 30:12 . App-69 .

strength = real power. Hebrew. geburah. Not the same word as in verses: Isaiah 30:2 , Isaiah 30:3 , but the same as in Isaiah 28:6 .

entries.title: flee . . . horses . . . shall ye flee.
entries.content:
flee . . . horses . . . shall ye flee. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia . Hebrew. nanus . . . sus . . . t'nusun, for emphasis.

swift . . . shall they. . . be swift. Figure of speech Paronomasia . Hebrew. kal . . . yikkallu, for emphasis; not a mere "play on words".

entries.title: One thousand shall flee.
entries.content:
One thousand shall flee. Reference to Pentateuch (Leviticus 26:8 .)

shall flee. The Figure of speech Ellipsis is correctly supplied from the next clause.

rebuke = threat.

ye flee = ye [all] flee.

a beacon = a pole, or mast.

ensign = flagstaff.

entries.title: be gracious
entries.content:
be gracious = show you favour, or grace.

have mercy upon you = show you compassion.

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

blessed = O the happinesses [of all, &c. ]. The first of three in Isaiah (Isaiah 32:20 ; Isaiah 56:2 ).

wait = look for.

entries.title: though.
entries.content:
though. Omit "though", and read it as a direct promise: "Jehovah will give you affliction [as] bread and adversity [as] water".

Lord* = Jehovah ( App-4 ). One of the 134 places where the Sopherim changed Jehovah of the primitive text for Adonai. Some codices, with three early printed editions, read "Jehovah" in the text.

yet shall not thy teachers = and thy teachers shall not.

corner. Hebrew occurs only here.

teachers. Perhaps plural of Majesty = thy great Teacher (i.e. Jehovah).

be removed into a corner = hide Himself.

see = be clearly seeing.

entries.title: covering.
entries.content:
covering. Hebrew. zapha ( zippoi ). Reference to Pentateuch. Occurs only here, Exodus 38:17 , Exodus 38:19 , and Numbers 16:38 , Numbers 16:39 . App-92 .

ornament. Hebrew. 'aphuddah (rendered ephod). Reference to Pentateuch. Occurs only here, Exodus 28:8 , and Exodus 39:5 .

entries.title: thy seed.
entries.content:
thy seed. Another reading (Ben Naphtali) is "thy land".

earth = ground, or soil.

entries.title: ear.
entries.content: ear. Old English = to plough: from Anglo-Saxon erian: and this from the Latin arare : the Aryan root AR entering into many words with a cognate reference. ARt (ploughing being the oldest art); oAR (with which the water is ploughed); ARtos(Greek for bread); eARth; ARatrum (Latin, a plough); ARare (to plough). The verb "ear" is found only here, Deuteronomy 21:4 , and 1 Samuel 8:12 . The noun "earing" occurs in Genesis 45:6 , and Exodus 34:21 .

entries.title: streams.
entries.content: streams. Hebrew. yiblei (from yabal = to bring, or conduct along). Occurs only here in the "former" portion, and only in Isaiah 44:4 , in the "latter" portion of Isaiah, where it is rendered "watercourses". App-79 .

entries.title: Behold.
entries.content:
Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos.

the name. See note on Psalms 20:1 .

entries.title: breath
entries.content:
breath = blast. Hebrew. ruach . See note on Isaiah 25:4 .

people = peoples.

entries.title: when a holy solemnity is kept.
entries.content:
when a holy solemnity is kept. Reference to Pentateuch. and the habitual keeping of the feasts there prescribed (Leviticus 23:2 , &c). See App-92 .

holy. See note on Exodus 3:6 .

the mountain of the LORD. See notes on Isaiah 2:3 , and Ezekiel 28:16 .

mighty One = Rock. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 32:4 , Deuteronomy 32:15 , Deuteronomy 32:18 , Deuteronomy 32:30 , Deuteronomy 32:31 ). Compare Isaiah 26:4 . App-92 .

entries.title: every place where the grounded staff, &c.
entries.content:
every place where the grounded staff, &c. = every stroke of the staff of doom, which, &c.

tabrets = drums. See note on 1 Samuel 10:5 . Hebrew. toph, forming the Figure of speech Paronomasia with Tophet in next verse, for emphasis.

shaking = tumult.

entries.title: Tophet
entries.content:
Tophet = the place of burning. In the valley of Hinnom, the place where continual fires consumed the refuse of Jerusalem. Compare Revelation 19:20 ; Revelation 20:10 .

the king = Moloch. See note on 1 Kings 11:7 .

breath. Hebrew. neshamah ( App-16 ). See note on Isaiah 2:22 .

entries.title: Woe.
entries.content:
Woe. The fourth of the six woes.

down. It is always "down" to Egypt, geographically and morally.

trust = confide. Hebrew. batah. App-69 .

the Holy One of Israel. See note on Isaiah 1:4 .Psalms 71:22 .

neither seek the LORD. Compare Isaiah 30:2 . Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 17:16 ). App-92 .

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. (with 'eth). App-4 .

entries.title: evil. evildoers.
entries.content:
evil. evildoers. Hebrew. ra'a' . App-44 .

iniquity. Hebrew. 'aven. App-44 .

entries.title: men, and not GOD.
entries.content:
men, and not GOD. Figure of speech Pleonasm . The statement put two ways for great emphasis (positive and negative).

men. Hebrew. 'ddam. App-14 .

GOD. Hebrew El = the mighty God. App-4 .

flesh, and not spirit. Figure of speech Pleonasm . See above.

spirit. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

entries.title: prey
entries.content:
prey = live prey.

multitude = crowd.

the LORD of hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 and 1 Samuel 1:3 .

for: or, over.

entries.title: As birds flying.
entries.content:
As birds flying. As birds hovering [covering and protecting their nest with their wings], so will, &c. The Figure of speech Ellipsis is to be thus supplied. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 32:11 ). App-92 .

defend = shield. The verb is found only in Isaiah's utterances (2 Kings 19:34 , 2 Kings 20:6 . 2Ki 31:5 ; 2Ki 37:35 ; 2Ki 38:6 ; and Zechariah 9:15 ; Zechariah 12:8 .

defending, &c. = shielding. Only used of God. Only here, 2Ki 19:34 ; 2 Kings 20:6 . Literally "[then there will be] a shielding, and He will rescue; a passing over [as in Egypt at the Passover], and he will cause to escape. "

passing over. Reference to Pentateuch (Ex. Isa 12:13 , Isa 12:23 , Isa 12:27 ). App-92 . This word is nowhere else used in this sense.

entries.title: Turn
entries.content:
Turn = Return.

children = sons.

entries.title: every man.
entries.content:
every man. Hebrew. 'Ish . App-14 .

idols = nothings.

entries.title: mighty man.
entries.content:
mighty man. Hebrew. 'ish. App-14 .

mean man. Hebrew. 'adam. App-14 .

discomfited = become tributaries.

entries.title: pass over.
entries.content: pass over. Not the same word as in Isaiah 31:5 (which is pasah). Here, Hebrew. 'abar, to cross over, or retreat.

entries.title: Behold.
entries.content:
Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos. App-6 .

a king. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 17:14 , Deuteronomy 17:16 ). App-92 .

in = for, in the interest of.

entries.title: And.
entries.content:
And. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton in verses: Isaiah 32:2-5 , emphasizing every detail.

man. Hebrew. 'ish. App-14 .

wind. Hebrew. ruach . App-9 .

rivers of water. Hebrew. palgei-mayim. Channels for irrigation in a garden. See notes on Proverbs 21:1 .Psalms 1:3 .

weary = thirsty.

entries.title: The heart also
entries.content: The heart also = And the heart: preserving the Figure of speech Polysyndeton (Isaiah 32:2 ).

entries.title: vile . . . villany.
entries.content:
vile . . . villany. Note the Figure of speech, Paronomasia ( App-6 ). Hebrew. nabal nebalah.

iniquity. Hebrew. 'aven . App-6

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah . App-4

soul. Hebrew. nephesh . App-13

entries.title: instruments also of the churl.
entries.content:
instruments also of the churl. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia . Hebrew. vekelay kelayv. English chattels of the churl.

evil. Hebrew. ra'a' . App-44 .

deviseth = counselleth.

wicked. Hebrew. rasha . App-44 .

devices = plans.

poor = wretched. Hebrew. anah . See note on Proverbs 6:11 .

needy = helpless, weak in will and wealth. Hebrew. ebyon . See note on Proverbs 6:11 .

entries.title: liberal
entries.content: liberal = noble: freehearted, freehanded.

entries.title: ye women.
entries.content:
ye women. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species), "women" being put for the whole nation, now reduced by sin to utter weakness; or, a special message, as in Isaiah 3:16-26 .

hear my voice. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 4:33 , Deuteronomy 4:36 ), App-92 .

careless = confident. Hebrew. batah . App-69 . Used here of self-confidence, in irony.

entries.title: pleasant fields
entries.content: pleasant fields =fields of desire. Figure of speech. Enallage . App-6

entries.title: forsaken
entries.content:
forsaken = neglected.

left. See note on "forsake", Isaiah 1:4 .

forever. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Whole), Put for a prolonged period. Note the limitation by the word "until" in the next verse.

entries.title: spirit.
entries.content:
spirit. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 . Compare Joel 2:28 . Ezekiel 36:25-27 .

poured. Hebrew. 'arah. Occurs in Isaiah 3:17 ; Isaiah 22:6 , and here in the "former" portion; and in Isaiah 53:12 , the "latter" portion.

entries.title: work
entries.content: work = tillage. assurance = confidence. Hebrew. b a t ah ( App-69 ) Same word as careless (Isaiah 32:9 ), but not in irony.

entries.title: hail, coming down.
entries.content: hail, coming down. Note the Figure of speech Paronomasia , for emphasis. Hebrew. ubarad beredeth; Eng. hail hailing.

entries.title: Blessed
entries.content: Blessed = O the happinesses of you, &c. The second of the three occurring in Isaiah. See note on Isaiah 30:18 . Compare Isaiah 56:2 .

entries.title: Woe.
entries.content:
Woe. The fifth of the six Woes. The Structure, above, will make this section quite clear, and show that the verses are not "out of place", or "disarranged".

that spoilest = thou plunderer.

dealest treacherously = thou traitor.

entries.title: arm.
entries.content:
arm. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause) for the strength and defense put forth by it.

every morning: i.e. continually.

entries.title: the people
entries.content:
the people = peoples.

the nations = nations.

entries.title: caterpiller
entries.content: caterpiller = locusts.

entries.title: is
entries.content: is = that [is].

entries.title: Behold.
entries.content:
Behold. Figure of speech. Asterismos . App-6 .

the ambassadors. Note the Figure of speech. Asyndeton ( App-6 ), inIsa 33:7-12.

entries.title: highways.
entries.content:
highways. See note on Isaiah 7:3 .

lie waste = are desolate. See note on Isaiah 1:7 .

wayfaring man = he that walketh along the path. See note on "path", Isaiah 2:3 .

man = mortal. Hebrew. 'enosh. App-14

entries.title: hewn down
entries.content:
hewn down = withered.

shake off. Hebrew. na'ar. A rare word. Occurs twice in the "former" portion (here, and Isaiah 33:15 ), and once in the "latter" portion (Isaiah 52:2 ). App-79 .

entries.title: saith the LORD
entries.content: saith the LORD = may Jehovah say. See note on Isaiah 1:11 .

entries.title: breath, as fire
entries.content: breath, as fire = breath as a fire. Hebrew. ruach.

entries.title: the people
entries.content:
the people = peoples.

burnings of lime: i.e. fuel for limekilns.

thorns cut up. These are the common fuel used in limekilns in Palestine.

entries.title: ye:
entries.content:
ye: i.e. the heathen.

what I have done: i.e. in the destruction of Sennacherib's army.

entries.title: fearfulness
entries.content:
fearfulness = trembling. Hebrew. r e 'adah. Only here in Isaiah; and elsewhere, only in Job 4:14 .Psalms 2:11 ; Psalms 48:6 .

surprised = seized.

Who . . . ? who . . . ? Figure of speech Erotesis . The answer implied being the negative.

among = for.

entries.title: He, &c.
entries.content:
He, &c. This is not the answer to Isaiah 33:14 , but the subject of the Promise in Isaiah 33:16 , "He. shall dwell on high". Hence it is emphatic. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 10:17 ; Deuteronomy 16:19 ; Deuteronomy 27:25 ).

hearing of = listening to.

blood = murderers. Figure of speech Metalepsis (of Subject), by which "blood" is first put for bloodshedding, and, secondly, bloodshedding put for those who shed it.

entries.title: the king.
entries.content:
the king. See Isaiah 33:22 .

far off = far stretching.

entries.title: scribe.
entries.content:
scribe. = the counter.

receiver = the weigher.

he that counted, &c. Referring to Sennacherib's besieging army.

entries.title: fierce, &c.
entries.content:
fierce, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 28:49 , Deuteronomy 28:50 ).

stammering = jabbering.

tongue. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause), for the language spoken by it.

entries.title: Look
entries.content:
Look = Gaze.

the city. Figure of speech Polyonymia.

solemnities = festal-days. Reference to Pentateuch, where the word frequently occurs (compare Leviticus 23 .Numbers 15 , &c).

tabernacle = tent. Hebrew. 'ohel. App-40 .

entries.title: gallant
entries.content: gallant = mighty, or noble.

entries.title: the lame take the prey.
entries.content: the lame take the prey. Referring to the spoil taken from the dead of the Assyrian host. See 2 Kings 19:35 .

entries.title: forgiven their iniquity.
entries.content: forgiven their iniquity. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 23:21 ; Exodus 32:32 .Numbers 14:19; Numbers 14:19 ).

entries.title: people
entries.content:
people = peoples.

world = the inhabited world. Hebrew. tebel.

all things, &c. = and all that is therein.

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

utterly destroyed = devoted to destruction, or, placed under a Divine ban.

entries.title: mountains shall be melted with their blood.
entries.content: mountains shall be melted with their blood. Figure of speech Hyperbole . So Isaiah 34:4 and Isaiah 34:5 .

entries.title: of My curse:
entries.content: of My curse: i.e. I have devoted.

entries.title: unicorns:
entries.content:
unicorns: or, rhinocerots. Hebrew. re'emin.

soaked = drunken. Figure of speech Hyperbole.

entries.title: of
entries.content: of = for.

entries.title: confusion.
entries.content:
confusion. See note on Isaiah 24:10 .

confusion . . . emptiness. Hebrew. tohu . . . bohu. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 1:2 ), "without form and void" = waste and desolate. Only there, here, and Jeremiah 4:23 beside. App-92 .

entries.title: come up in
entries.content: come up in = climb.

entries.title: screech owl.
entries.content:
screech owl. Hebrew. Lilith. Used to-day of any being of the night, as the English "bogy" is used. Charms are used against it to-day in Palestine.

a place, &c. = a roost.

entries.title: Seek
entries.content:
Seek = Search.

the book of the LORD. This proves there was a book in existence, which could be searched. See App-47 .

fail = be missing. Hebrew. 'adar. Not the same word as in Isaiah 19:5 (see note there). Occurs here in "former" portion, and Isaiah 40:26 in "latter"portion. See App-79 . Isaiah 35 is the sequel to this long series of Burdens (Isaiah 13:1 Isaiah 35:10 ) and Woes; it sets forth the future return of Israel.

entries.title: The wilderness, &c
entries.content:
The wilderness, &c .: i.e. the land of Edom referred to in Isaiah 34:9-16 . While Edom becomes a waste, the Land becomes a paradise; and the way of the return thither a peaceful highway.

shall be glad for them = shall rejoice over them.

them: i.e. the noisome creatures of Isaiah 34:14-16 , &c.

and = but; giving the contrast.

the desert shall rejoice, and blossom, & c. The description in this chapter leaves little to be interpreted. It requires only to be believed. No amount of spiritual blessing through the preaching of the Gospal can produce these physical miracles.

entries.title: Strengthen, &c.
entries.content: Strengthen, &c. Quoted in Hebrews 12:11 , Hebrews 12:12 .

entries.title: Then the eyes, &c.
entries.content: Then the eyes, &c. When Messiah came, these miracles (not miracles qua miracles) were the evidence that He had indeed come to save His People (Matthew 11:1-6 ), but they rejected Him. Hence, this with other similar prophecies are in abeyance. John had based his own claims on Isaiah 40:3 , while the Lord based His claims on Isaiah 35:5-6 .

entries.title: highway.
entries.content:
highway. See note on Isaiah 7:3 . Occurs only here.

The way, &c. = the holy road.

but, &c. : i.e. yet for those very persons it will exist.

err therein = go astray.

entries.title: No lion shall be there, &c.
entries.content: No lion shall be there, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Leviticus 26:6 ). App-92 .

entries.title: their heads.
entries.content:
their heads. Put by Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Part), for themselves.

sighing . See note on Isaiah 21:2 .Isaiah 40 takes up this theme, after the historical episode of Isaiah 36-39, which is necessary for the understanding of the references to the Assyrian invasion. For the general notes on this chapter see notes on 2 Kings 18:13 , 2 Kings 20:19 .

entries.title: it came to pass.
entries.content:
it came to pass. Note the insertion of these historical events in the midst of prophecy, corresponding with those concerning the reign of Ahaz. Compare 2 Kings 18:13 , 2 Kings 20:19 , on which Isaiah is not dependent, and 2 Chronicles 32:1-33 , which is not dependent on either (see App-56 ). This history is a proof of Isaiah's prophetic mission and gifts. History and prophecy are thus combined: for the latter is history foretold, and the former is (in this and many cases) prophecy fulfilled: the two accounts being perfectly independent.

in the fourteenth year: i.e. 628 B.C. See App-50 . pp Isa 59:60 . After Hezekiah's reformation (2 Chronicles 29:1 -- Isaiah 32:1 ). Samaria had been taken by Shalmaneser in Hezekiah's sixth year (2 Kings 18:10 ). The date (fourteenth year) no "error".

defenced cities = fortified cities.

and took them. See the list and number of them (forty-six) on Sennacherib's hexagonal cylinder in the British Museum. See App-67 .

entries.title: Rabshakeh:
entries.content:
Rabshakeh: or, "political officer". Probably a renegade Jew.

Lachish. Now Tell el Hesy , or Umm Lakis . See the work on the excavations there, published by the "Palestine Exploration Fund". Compare note on 2 Kings 18:17 , and 2 Kings 19:8 .

with a great army. Foretold in Isaiah 29:1-6 , as foretold in Isa 22:15-26 .

he stood. In the same spot where Isaiah stood with Ahaz twenty-eight years before. See Isaiah 7:3 .

highway. See note on Isaiah 7:3 .

entries.title: Eliakim.
entries.content:
Eliakim. See and Compare Isaiah 22:20-25 . The promise of Isaiah 22:20 , Isaiah 22:21 was already fulfilled.

house. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject), for household. Eliakim fulfils Shebna's office, as foretold in Isa 22:15-26 .

Shebna. See Isaiah 22:15 .

scribe: or, secretary. Title used of a state officer, first in 2 Samuel 8:17 . Connected with finance (2 Kings 22:3 ). Jeremiah 52:25 .

entries.title: the great king.
entries.content:
the great king. Contrast Psalms 47:2 .

trustest = hast confided. Hebrew. batah. App-69 . See Hezekiah's "Songs of the Degrees" (Psalms 121:3 ; Psalms 125:1 , Psalms 125:2 ; Psalms 127:1 ; Psalms 130:5-8 ; and App-67 ).

entries.title: I say, sayest thou.
entries.content:
I say, sayest thou. Some codices read "Thou sayest", as in 2 Kings 18:20 .

vain words = lip-talk. Hebrew word of lips.

entries.title: man.
entries.content: man. Hebrew. 'ish . App-14 .

entries.title: thou.
entries.content:
thou. Some codices read "ye", as in 2 Kings 18:22 .

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

is it not He . . . ? Manifesting Rabshakeh's ignorance.

entries.title: master.
entries.content: master. Hebrew. Adonai . App-4 .

entries.title: Egypt.
entries.content: Egypt. Hezekiah at first looked for help there (See Isaiah 20:3-6 ; Isaiah 30:2-5 ; 2 Kings 18:21 ).

entries.title: am I come up.
entries.content:
am I come up. As foretold twenty-eight years before (Isaiah 10:6-8 ).

If Rabshakeh knew of this, it shows the falsehood of "half the truth".

entries.title: Then said, &c.
entries.content:
Then said, &c. This led only to grosser insults.

Jews. The name by which the People were known of old, to foreigners. See note on Isaiah 36:2 . No proof of a later authorship. "Hebrew" is the later word for the language (Compare Isaiah 19:18 ).

entries.title: speak these words.
entries.content:
speak these words. See App-67 .

sit upon the wall = maintain their posts: i.e. till reduced to these extremities.

entries.title: this city.
entries.content: this city. Some codices, with two early printed editions, Septuagint, and Syriac, read "and this city": i.e. "this city".

entries.title: every one
entries.content: every one = man, as in Isaiah 36:6 .

entries.title: take you away.
entries.content:
take you away. As he did Israel (2 Kings 18:11 ).

wine = new wine. Hebrew. tirosh . App-27 .

bread. Put by Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Part), for all kinds of food.

Hath, &c. ? = [Reflect]: Hath, &c?

entries.title: Where:
entries.content: Where: or, Why, where. Some codices, with two early printed editions, read "Where then".

entries.title: went into the house of the Lord.
entries.content: went into the house of the Lord. See Hezekiah's reference to his love for, and use of, the Temple in his "Songs of the Degrees" (Psalms 122:1 , Psalms 122:9 ; Psalms 134:1 , Psalms 134:2 ; and App-67 ).

entries.title: elders of the priests.
entries.content: elders of the priests. These now added to the embassy. Joah absent.

entries.title: blasphemy
entries.content: blasphemy = reproach. Note the reference to this in Hezekiah's "Song of Degrees".

entries.title: Rabshakeh
entries.content:
Rabshakeh = the Rabshakeh. See note on Isaiah 36:2 .

lift up thy prayer. Note the reference to Hezekiah's "Song of the Degrees".

entries.title: Isaiah said.
entries.content: Isaiah said. The message in verses: Isaiah 37:6 , Isaiah 37:7 is shorter and calmer than the second.

entries.title: was departed from Lachish:
entries.content: was departed from Lachish: having raised the siege. See note on 2 Kings 18:17 ; 2 Kings 19:8 .

entries.title: he heard.
entries.content:
he heard. The "rumour" of Isaiah 37:7 .

Tirhakah. The Taracus of the inscriptions. The third and last of Manetho's twenty-sixth dynasty. This reference to the Ethiopian dynasty in Isaiah's time is an "undesigned coincidence".

Ethiopia. Judah's hope in Ethiopia was vain (See Isaiah 20:1-6 ).

entries.title: trustest
entries.content: trustest = confidest. Hebrew. batah.

entries.title: all lands
entries.content: all lands = all the earths: i.e. all such countries specially connected with Israel.

entries.title: Gozan, &c.
entries.content:
Gozan, &c. These places are all in Mesopotamia. and Bezeph. The Hebrew pointing connects this with the next clause.

children = sons.

entries.title: Hamath . . . Arphad . . . Sepharvaim.
entries.content: Hamath . . . Arphad . . . Sepharvaim. See notes on Isaiah 36:19 .

entries.title: spread it, &c.
entries.content: spread it, &c. See note on "lift up", &c. (Isaiah 37:4 ).

entries.title: LORD of Hosts.
entries.content:
LORD of Hosts. See note on Isaiah 1:9 , and 1 Samuel 1:3 .

God of Israel. See note on Isaiah 29:23 .

dwellest: or, sittest enthroned.

the. Hebrew He, the [God]. Compare 1 Kings 18:39 .

God. Hebrew. Elohim. (with Art.) = the [true] God.

made heaven and earth. Note the reference to this in Hezekiah's "Songs of the Degrees" (Psalms 121:1 , Psalms 121:2 ; Psalms 123:1 ; Psalms 124:8 ; Psalms 134:3 ; and App-67 (v)).

entries.title: ear . . . eyes.
entries.content: ear . . . eyes. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia.

entries.title: nations, and their countries.
entries.content: nations, and their countries. Hebrew. ha-arazoth . . . 'arzam : as in Isaiah 37:11 . The latter word put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the people inhabiting the lands. Note also the Figure of speech Paronomasia . Some codices read "nations, and their land".

entries.title: men's.
entries.content: men's. Hebrew. 'adam. App-14 .

entries.title: save us.
entries.content: save us. Some codices add "I (or, we) pray Thee", Compare 2 Kings 19:19 .

entries.title: thou hast prayed.
entries.content: thou hast prayed. See note on "lift up" (Isaiah 37:4 ).

entries.title: shaken = wagged.
entries.content: shaken = wagged. Denoting derision and scorn.

entries.title: the Holy One of Israel.
entries.content: the Holy One of Israel. See note on Isaiah 1:4 .

entries.title: LORD*.
entries.content:
